Willing suspension of disbelief is necessary to enjoy any non-documentary type movie these days.

I didn't mind the dust storm on Mars so much. Sure they could have used something more scientifically realistic to forward the plot to the point where "we left someone behind to save ourselves because we thought they were dead." But the dust storm was visually and mentally dramatic, so I think it was the best choice.

I saw Lucy a while ago, so it's not fresh in my mind. While I do remember thinking we already know the 10% thing is bullshit, it isn't unrealistic to entertain the possibility of having some crazy powers from using more of your brain.

Plus half the fun of science-fiction is the fiction aspect.
I like how near the end of the movie they mention how Mars' atmosphere is so thin that all you need is hab canvas to launch the mav into space.
I think you make a good point

I used to be a stickler for these things, but these days I'm happy as long as the world within the movie/book/game is internally consistent. 100% scientific accuracy isn't even possible, since we're constantly getting new data and what was fact even a few years ago is already being tweaked and fine-tuned as more data and better experiments are conducted. Of course, that doesn't change the fact that the "10%" thing is a myth and that there isn't enough atmosphere on Mars for that kind of storm, but you know what I mean.

I haven't seen Lucy but was the 10% idea framed as a sci-fi what-if? Perhaps it simply went over people's heads or they had wrong expectations and viewed it through the wrong lenses, as it were. I suppose the Martian thing is simply because people don't know about that but knew about the 10% and the level of suspension of disbelieve in regards to the Martian (10% is harder to put aside than dust storms being less dangerous).

What annoyed me about the movie was that I could see it potentially reinforcing the 10% myth in the minds of the public. I just wish they'd chosen some other path to go down because it was otherwise a really fun movie which I did genuinely enjoy, Morgan Freeman's speeches full of pseudoscience misinfo notwithstanding.

I was willing to suspend my disbelief during Lucy, the real problem with that movie was that the characters were flat and unengaging, it became boring because the characters were hard to care about which it turn makes it difficult to keep disbelief suspended. Whereas in the Martian Matt Damon was charismatic enough to keep me invested, much easier to sustain suspended disbelief.

It also does Lucy no favors that many people are already annoyed at the 10% lie on account of having heard it so many time from idiots who actually believe it. Whereas with the Martian the average person doesn't know or care enough about the Martian atmosphere for the premise to bother them, I've never had an idiot try to sell me on some woo self help book which promised it would help me unlock the other 90% of my Martian atmosphere if you know what I'm saying.

What annoyed me was Morgan Freeman being wasted and the fucking b footage of wildlife. The idea of intelligence warping reality was great and could have been used effectively, but it ended up being kind of meh.

The entire premise of Lucy hangs on the fact that people supposedly use 10% of their brainpower, and protagonist uses more. It's flawed and bullshit from start to finish, and the plot is soaked in misinformation.

Dust storm in The Martian is a one time event. Sure, it kickstarts the actual plot, but it's mentioned only at the beginning, and never comes back.

When I watch a movie, I assume everything is fiction although it should stick to the same level of fiction within each movie. By that, I mean don't just introduce aliens in a sci-fi thriller (e.g., 'Knowing' with Nicholas Cage).
